title: P-N Junction Explorer
description: Four linked plots for an abrupt silicon p-n junction: the band diagram with Fermi or quasi-Fermi levels, the charge density and electric field of the depletion approximation, the current density against voltage split into diffusion and recombination-generation parts, and the carrier concentrations on each side. Sliders set the applied voltage and the doping on each side, and a menu sets the temperature.
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: semiconductor physics

chapter_title: P-N Junction: Equilibrium, Bias, and the Ideal Diode

educational.topic: Electrostatics and current-voltage characteristic of the p-n junction
learningObjectives: Explain how forward and reverse bias change the depletion width
Calculate the built-in potential and depletion width for given doping values
Identify which current component dominates at a given forward voltage
Predict how the current-voltage curve changes with doping and temperature
prerequisites: Drift, diffusion, and the Einstein relation

pedagogical.interactionPattern: Parameter sliders with four linked real-time plots, a readout strip, and a worked-calculation panel
pedagogical.instructionalStrategy: Predict-test-observe: students predict the change in depletion width, field, and current, then check against the linked plots
assessmentOpportunities: Compute the built-in potential and depletion width by hand and compare with the readout
Find the voltage at which diffusion current overtakes recombination current
Explain why the reverse current rises slowly with reverse voltage

equations: W = sqrt(2 eps_s (V_bi - V)/q * (N_A + N_D)/(N_A N_D)), N_A x_p = N_D x_n
J_s = q n_i^2 (D_p/(L_p N_D) + D_n/(L_n N_A))
assumptions: eps_s = 11.7 eps_0; n_i(300 K) = 9.65e9 cm^-3; N_C, N_V = 2.86e19, 3.10e19 cm^-3 scaled as T^1.5; Varshni E_g(T)
Mobility from 300 K doping fits (Chapter 8 for electrons, Arora et al. 1982 for holes); D = mu kT/q
Minority carrier and generation lifetimes fixed at 1 microsecond
limitations: Depletion approximation and low-level injection; plots stop at V_bi - 0.05 V
No series resistance, breakdown, or tunneling
Mobility temperature dependence and dopant freeze-out are neglected
